overview: This bill, the America the Beautiful Act, renews a fund created in 2020 to fix the repair backlog at national parks, wildlife refuges, national forests, other public lands, and Bureau of Indian Education schools. Deposits from federal onshore energy revenue would resume for 2027 through 2031, and the fund would also receive money from a new extra entrance fee for foreign visitors to national parks that charge entry (not U.S. citizens, nationals, or green card holders) and from licensing Interior Department trademarks and other intellectual property. The bill sets minimum shares for non-road repairs at each agency, bars using the money to buy land, pay staff bonuses, or close Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management roads, and requires the administration to submit yearly project lists to Congress or risk delayed funding. It also aims to speed up projects by streamlining environmental and historic preservation reviews, raising small-purchase limits, and allowing some no-bid contracts with states, tribes, nonprofits and park concessioners. As of June 17, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say it keeps steady money flowing to repair crumbling roads, buildings, water systems and visitor facilities on public lands, while asking foreign tourists to contribute and adding rules to get projects done faster and more transparently.
against: Critics say faster environmental reviews and no-bid contracts could weaken oversight and protections, and a surcharge on foreign visitors could discourage tourism in gateway communities that depend on it.
